headline: Prices for a typical Vaughan home are about 5% lower than a year ago, and the Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% on October 28. New condo sales are weak, and few new projects are starting. Many VMC projects are still waiting for approval.

status.label: Fewer units under construction
status.explanation: Vaughan has 3,144 homes under construction, down from 3,588 a year ago. 89 VMC development applications are active, but none were received in the last 180 days.

status.label: New condo sales weak, recovering
status.explanation: Across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, new condo sales were 246 in the first quarter of 2026. They rose to 702 in the second quarter. In Vaughan, 57 resale condo apartments sold in October.

status.label: Prices lower than last year
status.explanation: The typical Vaughan home costs $1,106,600, down 5.46% in a year. A typical condo apartment is $504,900, down 6.51%. Prices are Vaughan-wide, not VMC only.

status.label: Rents flat, vacancy 2.4%
status.explanation: The average rent in the wider Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, down from $1,762 in 2024. The vacancy rate was 2.4%. This is a wider area than the VMC.

status.label: Rates up, charges down
status.explanation: The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% from 2.25% a year ago, because of high energy prices. York Region cut its development charges, which are fees on new buildings.

personas.bottom_line: Prices are lower than a year ago, but borrowing costs have not fallen.

points.text: A typical Vaughan condo apartment is $504,900, down 6.51% from a year ago and well below its March 2022 peak of $864,400.
The posted 5-year mortgage rate is 6.19%, up from 6.09% a year ago. Posted rates are higher than the rates most people negotiate.
The Bank of Canada raised its rate on October 28, saying it acted so high energy prices do not spread broadly.

watch: The December 9 Bank of Canada decision

personas.bottom_line: Rents in the wider zone have been flat, and more rental choice may be coming.

points.text: The average rent in the Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, compared with $1,917 in the Toronto area.
The vacancy rate was 2.4%. A higher rate usually means more choice for renters.
Vaughan finished 6,368 homes in 2025, which adds to supply.

personas.bottom_line: Townhouses and detached homes cost less than a year ago, but they are still pricey.

points.text: A typical Vaughan townhouse is $714,500, down 8.85% in a year.
A typical detached home is $1,482,000, down 5.35%.
The 4.8 months of inventory means buyers have more time to decide than in tight markets.

watch: New school and park plans for the VMC

personas.bottom_line: Sellers face lower prices and more competing listings than a year ago.

points.text: Homes sold for about 97% of the asking price in October, with 1,219 active listings.
The typical home price of $1,106,600 is 30% below the March 2022 peak of $1,587,400.
The mechanical baseline puts a typical home near $1,087,732 in April 2027, with a wide 80% range of $984,235 to $1,194,248.

personas.bottom_line: Prices and rents are flat to lower, so the risks are high and the picture is mixed.

points.text: Condo prices fell 6.51% in a year, while average rents in the wider zone were slightly lower.
A record 4,295 new condos in the Toronto area were finished but unsold as of the first quarter of 2026.
The posted 5-year mortgage rate is 6.19%, which raises the cost of borrowing.

personas.bottom_line: A smaller home may cost much less, but timing the sale is hard.

points.text: A typical Vaughan condo apartment is $504,900, compared with $1,482,000 for a detached home.
Condo apartments had 419 active listings in October and 57 sales, so buyers have plenty of choice.
Many VMC towers are under review, so more condo choices may arrive over several years.

scenarios.name: optimistic
scenarios.summary: Inflation cools, rates ease, and buyers return. Prices stabilize and new projects restart.

assumptions.assumption: Stops rising and moves back to 2.25% or lower by late 2027.
Keep rising from the second-quarter 2026 level of 702 sales in the Toronto and Hamilton area.
Lower development charges help more projects reach construction.

drivers.text: Lower development charges cut the cost of building.
New condo sales rose 52% from a year earlier in the second quarter.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.summary: Prices stay flat to slightly lower. Few new starts keep supply tight later, while projects already underway finish.

assumptions.assumption: Stays at about 2.5% through mid-2027, with the next decision on December 9, 2026.
Vaughan starts stay near recent levels, about 1,652 over 12 months.

drivers.text: There are 89 active applications, which shows developers still plan to build.

scenarios.name: pessimistic
scenarios.summary: Higher rates and unsold condos push prices lower and delay projects.

assumptions.assumption: Rises above 2.5% if inflation, now about 3%, keeps climbing.
The count of completed, unsold new condos stays above the first-quarter record of 4,295.
Fall toward the bottom of the baseline range, about $398,567 by October 2027.

drivers.text: Inflation near 3% could push rates up again.
No new project launches happened in the first quarter of 2026, which delays future supply.

baseline_views.reason: Prices are down 5.46% in a year, and a rate rise offsets lower fees. The baseline is a fair guess.
No cited evidence supports a departure from the baseline over 12 months.
The baseline assumes no change, but condo prices are falling 6.51% a year and the unsold condo backlog is record-high.
The baseline already expects a decline to $484,890, which matches the current trend.
Starts were 1,243 so far in 2026 against 968 in all of 2025, so about 1,650 is reasonable.
Apartment starts are lumpy, and no evidence suggests a clear change from the baseline of 1,508.
Units under construction fell from 3,588 to 3,144 in a year. Finishing projects offset slow starts.
Rents in the zone were $1,726 in 2025 with 2.4% vacancy, so little change is expected.

events.title: Bank of Canada raises its rate by 0.25 points to 2.5%
events.impact: Higher rates make borrowing cost more, which can weigh on buyers. The Bank said it acted so high energy prices do not spread through the economy.

events.title: Next Bank of Canada rate decision
events.impact: This decision will show whether rates keep rising. Inflation has been around 3% since April.

events.title: York Region's new development charges take effect
events.impact: Fees on new buildings fell between 2% and 9% for homes. Lower fees may help projects go ahead.

events.title: No new condo projects launched in the Toronto area in Q1
events.impact: A record 4,295 finished new condos were unsold. Developers have little reason to start new towers.

events.title: New condo sales rose 52% in the second quarter
events.impact: Sales rebounded to 702 units, which is a small number. The building pipeline shrank by 37% in a year.

watch_list.threshold: Another rate rise on December 9, 2026, or a hold at 2.5%
watch_list.why: Rates shape mortgage costs and buyer demand.
The Bank has said it expects inflation near 3.5% by year end, and higher inflation can lead to more rate increases.

watch_list.signal: Months of resale inventory in Vaughan
watch_list.why: More inventory gives buyers power and can lower prices.

watch_list.threshold: Launches resume and sales stay above 702 a quarter

watch_list.why: New applications show developers are planning more projects.
Shows if building activity is shrinking or recovering.

evidence.quote: Governing Council decided to increase the policy rate to reduce the risk that continuing high energy prices spread broadly
The Bank of Canada today increased its target for the overnight rate by 25 basis points
The next scheduled date for announcing the overnight rate target is December 9, 2026.
CPI inflation has been around 3% since April and is expected to rise to about 3½% by the end of the year.
Region-wide DC rates decrease between 2% and 9% for residential development
The updated 2026 Region-wide Bylaw and Nobleton Bylaw was in effect as of Thursday, May 21, 2026.
A record-high 4,295 new condos were completed and unsold as of Q1,
For the first time in at least 30 years, there were no new project launches during the quarter.
In Q1-2026, 246 new condominiums were sold in the Greater Toronto Hamilton Area (GTHA),
New condominium apartment sales in the Greater Toronto Hamilton Area (GTHA) increased 52% annually to 702 units in Q2-2026
combined pre-construction and under-construction inventory falling to 48,710 units in Q2 — down 37% from a year earlier
